title: InPlacePodVerticalScalingSchedulerPreemption: Beta graduation criteria
body:
This is an umbrella issue to track required changes prior to beta promotion of InPlacePodVerticalScalingSchedulerPreemption (KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5836)

It is a combination of the initial beta criteria we scoped out on https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5836, as well as important considerations identified during code review of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140000.

### KEP Beta Criteria
- [ ] Define and implement relevant metrics and events.
- [ ] Define, implement, and link additional comprehensive integration tests in the KEP.
- [ ] Clarify and design co-existence mechanics for workload-aware scheduling (e.g., group-wide coordinated preemption or evaluating pod group health before preempting).
- [ ] Address scenarios where a preemption victim's grace period exceeds the time window allocated for executing the resize operation (e.g., VPA's fallback time limit).
- [ ] Finalize the approach to prevent "double preemption" across scheduler restarts and long grace periods (e.g., evaluating `nominatedNodeName` vs. checking `spec.nodeName` in `DefaultPreemption`).
- [ ] Evaluate whether to solve the risk of additional unnecessary preemption by aligning `NodeResourcesFit` resource accounting logic with the Kubelet's logic (`max(desired, allocated, actual)`) when evaluating deferred pods.
- [ ] Ensure the Deferred resize scheduling cycle includes resources from `pod.status.nodeAllocatableResourceClaimStatuses` if KEP-5517 Alpha2 (DRA) is implemented.

### Implementation PR Follow-ups & Technical Items (PR #140000)
- [ ] **[Node Resources Fit Delta Calculation (`max(0, ...)` Handling)](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140000#discussion_r3608175391):** Re-evaluate the `NodeResourcesFit` resource accounting delta logic when calculating a deferred pod's target resource footprint. 
- [ ] **[Observability & Autoscaler Integration](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140000#discussion_r3613628887):** Surface scheduling preemption failure reasons (via Events, appending details/reasons to status conditions like `Deferred`, or updating `PodResizePending`) so users and possibly autoscaling controllers (like VPA) can determine why space could not be made. Ensure that kubelet handles such changes (including consideration for version skew). 
- [ ] **[Binding Phase Refactoring](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140000#discussion_r3609589583):** Evaluate progressing deferred pods through the binding cycle (implementing `Bind()` and updating `PodResizePending`) instead of using `Permit` phase rejections while waiting for Kubelet actuation. This removes waiting pods from the scheduling queue and allows eliminating unnecessary `ScaleUp` queueing hints in `NodeResourcesFit` [(discussion on ScaleUp QHints)](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140000#discussion_r3609619666).
- [ ] **[Framework Extension Point (`IsResponsible`)](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140000#discussion_r3609616086):** Evaluate introducing a general scheduler extension point interface (`IsResponsible(pod)`) to clean up runtime plugin execution and avoid individual `IsPodResizeDeferred(pod)` checks across multiple plugins.
- [ ] **[Integration Test Refactoring](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140000#discussion_r3614974843):** Refactor new integration tests (`TestDeferredResizeNodePreemptionPolicy` and `TestDeferredResizeQueueingHandlers`) to be table-driven and consider reusing `CoreResourceEnqueueTestCase`.

title: APF queueset can panic ("slice bounds out of range") and crash the apiserver when a queue holding a lingering request is removed after a DesiredNumQueues reduction
body:
### What happened?

In `staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/util/flowcontrol/fairqueuing/queueset/queueset.go`, a request that has finished its main service but still occupies seats during its `AdditionalLatency` (a "lingering" request, e.g. a mutating request whose work estimate reserves seats for its watch fan-out) is removed from `requestsExecuting` immediately in `finishRequestLocked`, while releasing its seats and calling `removeQueueIfEmptyLocked` is deferred to an `EventAfterDuration` callback that fires `AdditionalLatency` later.

`removeQueueIfEmptyLocked` decides whether to drop an excess queue using:

```go
if len(qs.queues) > qs.qCfg.DesiredNumQueues &&
    r.queue.requestsWaiting.Length() == 0 &&
    r.queue.requestsExecuting.Len() == 0 {   // does not check seatsInUse
    qs.queues = removeQueueAndUpdateIndexes(qs.queues, r.queue.index)
    ...
}
```

It does not check `seatsInUse`. So if `DesiredNumQueues` has been reduced (excess queues draining by attrition) and a queue Q holds a lingering request `r` plus another request `s`, then when `s` finishes it sees Q as empty (0 waiting, 0 executing — `r` was already removed from the executing set) and removes Q, even though `r`'s seats still linger. `removeQueueAndUpdateIndexes` only fixes up the `index` field of the *kept* queues, so the removed Q keeps a now-stale `index`, and `r.queue` still points at it. When `r`'s lingering timer later fires, its deferred `removeQueueIfEmptyLocked(r)` calls `removeQueueAndUpdateIndexes(qs.queues, <stale index>)` a second time:

- if the stale index is out of range for the now-shorter slice, `queues[index+1:]` panics with `slice bounds out of range`;
- otherwise it removes a different, live queue, silently corrupting fairness/seat accounting and stranding that flow's requests.

The panic runs in the goroutine spawned by `eventclock.Real.EventAfterDuration` (`go func(){ t := <-ch; f(t) }()`), which has no `recover`, so it crashes the whole apiserver process.

### What did you expect to happen?

The queue should not be removed while a lingering request still holds seats in it, and it should never be removed twice.


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Unit-level, with the queueset's fake event clock (test in `package queueset`):

1. Build a queuing queueset with `DesiredNumQueues: 3, HandSize: 1` and ample concurrency.
2. `StartRequest` two requests with the same hash (so they share queue index 2): `r` with `WorkEstimate{InitialSeats:1, FinalSeats:1, AdditionalLatency: time.Second}` (lingering) and `s` normal.
3. Reconfigure to `DesiredNumQueues: 1` (the three queues remain, draining by attrition).
4. `r.Finish(...)` then `s.Finish(...)`.
5. Advance the fake clock past `AdditionalLatency`.

Result on current master: `panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [3:2]` in `removeQueueAndUpdateIndexes`, from the lingering timer callback. (A regression test is attached; it panics before the fix and passes after.)


### Anything else we need to know?

Trigger requires an operator to reduce a PriorityLevelConfiguration's `queuing.queues` (so excess queues are draining) together with the right concurrent traffic and timing, so probability is low; but the consequence (apiserver panic, or silent fairness corruption) is severe, and it is reachable through supported configuration. This is a robustness bug on configuration change, not a security issue (no unprivileged trigger, no escalation).

Fix: add `&& r.queue.seatsInUse == 0` to the `removeQueueIfEmptyLocked` guard so a queue is not removed while a lingering request still holds its seats; the queue is then removed exactly once, by the lingering request's own deferred call after its seats are released.

title: [Flaking Test][[sig-redacted]] WorkloadAwarePreemption should preempt partial group with Single disruption mode by a pod group
E2E Test Flakiness: API Server Timeouts, Silent Failures, and Resource Cleanup Issues
body:
The e2e test framework has several patterns that cause flakiness, silent resource leaks, and hard-to-debug failures, especially in disruptive tests that restart API servers or control plane components. PR 137832 addresses these across 13 files (185 additions, 41 deletions), touching [sig-redacted], apps, cloud-provider, network, node, storage, and testing.

Error suppression hides resource leaks. Across the test suite, cleanup code discards errors from Delete calls. In test/e2e/apimachinery/aggregator.go, the cleanupSampleAPIServer function has 10 such calls (APIService, Deployment, Secret, Service, ServiceAccount, RoleBinding, ClusterRoleBinding, ClusterRole) all silently swallowed. Same pattern in test/e2e/apimachinery/apply.go (4 deployments/pods), test/e2e/apps/rc.go (DeleteCollection), and test/e2e/apps/statefulset.go (ConfigMaps in defer blocks). When these fail, resources leak into subsequent tests with zero trace of what went wrong.

No retry on transient API server errors. GetControlPlaneNodes in test/e2e/framework/util.go calls Nodes().List() and immediately fails on any error. During disruptive tests (daemon restarts, etcd failure injection), the API server is expected to be briefly unreachable. The same issue exists in allNodesReady at test/e2e/framework/node/helper.go and RestartNodes at test/e2e/common/util.go. A transient connection refused or 503 kills the entire test instead of retrying. The fix introduces IsRetryableAPIError which checks for connection refused/reset, server timeout, 429, 503, 500, and unexpected server errors, plus a new WaitForControlPlaneNodes that wraps the listing in a polling loop with retry-on-transient logic.

Healthz returns 200 before daemon is ready. RestartDaemonConfig.waitUp in test/e2e/apps/daemon_restart.go considers the daemon ready when /healthz returns HTTP 200. After a kubelet restart, the health endpoint can report ok while kubelet is still recovering. Logs show errors, pods are not yet scheduled. The fix adds verifyDaemonReadiness which SSHes into the node and checks the last 20 lines of /var/log/kubelet.log for error patterns before declaring readiness.

Goroutines not gracefully stopped. In test/e2e/apps/daemon_restart.go, a cache.NewInformer controller is started with go controller.Run(backgroundCtx.Done()). The cleanup calls cancel() but does not wait for the controller goroutine to finish. The fix replaces this with a dedicated stopCh channel and DeferCleanup that closes the channel then sleeps 100ms to allow graceful shutdown.

PVC deletion races with pod references. DeleteAllStatefulSets in test/e2e/framework/statefulset/rest.go has a TODO comment about not checking whether pods still reference PVCs before deleting them. The current code deletes PVCs immediately, which can fail or leave orphaned PVs when pods are still running. The fix lists pods, checks volume references, and only deletes PVCs that are not in use, with foreground propagation.

Duplicated control plane filtering. GetControlPlaneNodes and WaitForControlPlaneNodes both contain the same node filtering logic (check for control-plane label and NoSchedule taint). The second commit extracts this into a shared filterControlPlaneNodes helper.

All changes are in e2e test code, no user-facing impact.

Related issues:
- 109600: prevent the Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred()) and ExpectNoError(err) anti-pattern in e2e tests (same category of error handling problems)
- 86253: sample-apiserver returns error instead of falling back to second Accept type (directly affects the aggregator.go test modified in this PR)
- 135285: GOAWAY are not handled gracefully in apiserver when aggregating (related network error handling)
- 105536: Orphaned pod found, but error not a directory occurred when trying to remove the volumes dir (related resource cleanup issue)

title: Memory Manager AllocatePod re-applies restored pod allocations after kubelet restart
body:
### What happened?

With pod-scope Topology Manager and `PodLevelResourceManagers` enabled, the static Memory Manager restores pod-level assignments from its checkpoint when kubelet starts. The existing Pods then go through admission again, and Topology Manager calls `AllocatePod` with `AddOperation`.
﻿
`AllocatePod` does not check whether the Pod already has a restored allocation. It calculates the request again and applies it to a machine state which already includes that Pod's reservation.
﻿
Depending on the remaining capacity, this can:
﻿
- reject an existing Pod during post-restart admission because its own allocation is no longer considered free;
- extend or change the previously selected NUMA affinity;
- reserve the same memory a second time, reducing `Free` and increasing `Reserved` and `NumberOfAssignments` again.
﻿
The Pod and container block entries are overwritten, but the additional machine-state accounting remains and is checkpointed.
﻿
﻿

### What did you expect to happen?

Pod-level Memory Manager allocation should be idempotent across kubelet restart.

When a complete allocation for the Pod has been restored from the checkpoint, post-restart admission should preserve the existing pod allocation, container assignments, NUMA affinity, and machine state. It should not consume capacity again or reject the Pod because of its own reservation.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

A deterministic unit test can extend `TestMemoryManagerRestoreState`:

1. Enable `PodLevelResources` and `PodLevelResourceManagers`.
2. Configure static Memory Manager with pod-scope Topology Manager.
3. Create a Guaranteed Pod with pod-level memory requests and limits and one container.
4. Start Memory Manager and call `AllocatePod` once.
5. Save the pod blocks, container blocks, and machine state.
6. Recreate Memory Manager with the same checkpoint directory to simulate kubelet restart.
7. Start the new manager and verify that the state was restored.
8. Call `AllocatePod` again with `AddOperation`, as post-restart admission does.
9. Verify that the call succeeds and all restored state remains unchanged.

With the current implementation, step 8 either accounts the Pod again or fails when there is not enough unreserved capacity to satisfy the same request a second time.

Using a single-container Pod keeps this reproducer separate from pod-scope hint regeneration behavior for multi-container Pods.

title: kube-apiserver: request can hang for 40–90s when its etcd transport is recycled mid-flight (grpc-go v1.72.2 bug, fixed in v1.77.0; affects release-1.34/1.35)
body:
### What happened?

In our CI environment (Calico Felix functional tests, which start a fresh kube-apiserver per test), a LIST of a CRD hung inside the apiserver for 13+ seconds while identical LISTs from other clients, through the same apiserver, succeeded within 300 ms. The stuck request was still blocked on its first attempt of an etcd KV/Range RPC when the client gave up:

```
{"level":"warn","logger":"etcd-client","caller":"v3@v3.6.5/retry_interceptor.go:65","msg":"retrying of unary invoker failed","target":"etcd-endpoints://0xc004ab9680/[...]:2379","method":"/etcdserverpb.KV/Range","attempt":0,"error":"rpc error: code = Canceled desc = context canceled"}
E ... timeout.go:140] "Post-timeout activity" ... method="GET" path="/apis/crd.projectcalico.org/v1/globalnetworksets"
```

etcd (single node, v3.5.24) was healthy throughout: no slow-apply or read-index warnings, and it served all other requests, including the same LIST from other clients, in milliseconds.

The hung request was the first request ever for that CRD on the freshly started apiserver. First requests trigger lazy creation of the CRD's storage, including a new etcd client (one per CRD - #111476). The hang coincided with a burst of transport churn from ~14 CRD storages being created at once:

```
W ... grpc: addrConn.createTransport failed to connect ... Err: connection error: desc = "error reading server preface: read tcp [...]: use of closed network connection"
W ... grpc: addrConn.createTransport failed to connect ... Err: "transport: failed to write client preface: write tcp [...]: use of closed network connection"
W ... grpc: addrConn.createTransport failed to connect ... Err: "transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp [...]: operation was canceled"
```

### What did you expect to happen?

All requests for that list serviced promptly.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Repeatedly hammer the list CR path on freshly started API server.  It is probabilistic and infrequent.

### Anything else we need to know?

Upstream fix (assuming RCA below is correct)

- grpc/grpc-go#8425 ("Transport close blocks on unresponsive reader"), fixed by grpc/grpc-go#8534 ("transport: Invoke net.Conn.SetReadDeadline in http2_client.Close"), released in grpc-go v1.77.0. Related hardening: grpc/grpc-go#8615 (pickfirstleaf stuck in IDLE), released in v1.76.0.
- Neither was backported to grpc-go 1.72.x.
- kubernetes master picked up the fix incidentally via routine dependency maintenance (#136227, grpc v1.78.0; then #137906, v1.79.3), so 1.36 is fixed. release-1.35 (through v1.35.7) and release-1.34 still vendor grpc-go v1.72.2.

Potential root cause (from Claude): 

internal/transport/http2_client.go strands in-flight RPCs when a transport leaves service:

- Close(): calls t.onClose(...) first the subchannel immediately reports the transport dead and new RPCs move to a fresh transport — then waits for GOAWAY write, then blocks on <-t.readerDone with no deadline, and only after that errors the in-flight streams. If the dying connection goes mute (no FIN/RST reaches the reader), in-flight streams wait indefinitely.
- GracefulClose(): calls t.onClose(...) and then waits for active streams to drain with no deadline; in-flight streams are never errored at all.

So an RPC that lands on a transport just as it is being recycled is stranded on attempt 0: the etcd retry interceptor never sees the attempt finish, so it never retries, while every new RPC succeeds on the replacement transport. The etcd client defaults to WaitForReady(true), so nothing bounds the attempt client-side. The only recovery paths are the etcd client keepalive configured in storagebackend/factory/etcd3.go (30s ping / 10s timeout → ~40–86s) or the HTTP request's own context ending (server --request-timeout, or the caller disconnecting — which is what we observed).

Two things make first-requests-to-CRDs a reliable trigger window: per-CRD lazy storage creation churns subchannels exactly

title: Add back `admissioninitializer.WantsAuthorizer` for v1.37
body:
As part of implementing [Conditional Authorization](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5681), in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138801 we did a literal rename from 

```go
if wants, ok := plugin.(WantsAuthorizer); ok {
	wants.SetAuthorizer(i.authorizer)
}
```

to

```go
if wants, ok := plugin.(WantsUnconditionalAuthorizer); ok {
	wants.SetUnconditionalAuthorizer(i.authorizer)
}
```

using a fully mechanical rename, with `authorizer.UnconditionalAuthorizer` corresponding to the authorizer interface that existed in v1.36, and `authorizer.Authorizer` growing new capabilities in v1.37.

The intention was to add `admissioninitializer.WantsAuthorizer` in a subsequent PR as a clean diff to show new usage of new features. 

If commit https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/833f712b4259a5a18a4bd4aee078f422dd3ec776, admission plugins that provide `SetAuthorizer(authorizer.Authorizer)` in v1.36 would either:

a) get a compile error in v1.37 if they locked their implementation like `var _ admissioninitializer.WantsAuthorizer = fooPlugin{}`
b) fail silently at runtime during `ValidateInitialization() error` as `SetAuthorizer` wouldn't be called

...until the admission plugin performed the same rename.

This code was initially part of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137633 (and its prefactor https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140715), but given this larger feature PR will not be part of v1.37, I propose to break out the commit to a dedicated PR, which targets v1.37 as a bug fix, to not break existing clients that depended on `admissioninitializer.WantsAuthorizer`.

title: kubelet: serialized pod status sync causes unnecessary cross-pod serialization
body:
### What would you like to be added?

The bottleneck in high throughput pod churn (> 5 pods / second / node) seems to be the status update from kubelet.  Other controllers rely on this update, so even if the container has started it is not necessarily visible externally.

There are low-hanging opportunities for efficiency improvement: It does a GET before each update, it runs multiple updates for a pod start (though these already coalesce under load), and it does all operations in series on a single worker goroutine, where a batch of pod status updates blocks the next batch.

Proposed fixes:

- Parallelize status syncs with per-pod ordering preserved . This is what #124596 was addressing (closed by triage bot).
- Eliminate the GET — serve the precondition check from the informer/last-known state (also proposed in #123875).
- Two-tier queue — first-time-Ready and deletion-releasing syncs ahead of lower-importance updates; per-pod coalescing means we are already dropping these updates under moderate load - there's no guarantee that clients will observe them as individual updates.

I have a reproducible benchmark harness (kOps + load generator + per-pod tracing across watch/journal/containerd), full artifacts for every number above, and I'm happy to help revive #124596 or review/test an alternative.

If it's helpful, I can also try to figure out how to run the agent-sandbox stress-test on demand against k/k, I think the test is pretty good at capturing a lot of information in a machine readable format, and then generating a report in a human-readable format!

### What would you like to be added?

The Kubelet configuration validation for CPU Manager (`CPUManagerPolicyOptions`) and Topology Manager (`TopologyManagerPolicyOptions`) should support Kubernetes version emulation through `CompatibilityVersion`.

Currently, policy options are validated against static, compile-time lists (`alphaOptions`, `betaOptions`, and `stableOptions`). Instead, validation should determine whether an option is available based on its lifecycle at the emulated Kubernetes version.

Specifically, configuration validation should:

- Evaluate policy option availability using versioned lifecycle information.
- Compare the option's maturity stage against the current emulation version (`DefaultFeatureGate.EmulationVersion()`).
- Respect the corresponding feature gates for that emulated version (for example, `CPUManagerPolicyAlphaOptions`, `CPUManagerPolicyBetaOptions`, and their Topology Manager equivalents).
- Reject policy options that were not available or enabled in the target emulated release.

This would make CPU Manager and Topology Manager configuration validation consistent with the semantics of `CompatibilityVersion`.

### Why is this needed?

`CompatibilityVersion` allows users to run a newer Kubernetes binary while emulating the behavior of an older Kubernetes release. This is important for upgrades, rollbacks, and version-skew testing.

Today, CPU Manager and Topology Manager policy options are validated against static lists compiled into the binary rather than the emulated version. As a result, options introduced or promoted in later Kubernetes releases can be incorrectly accepted when emulating an older version.

For example, `prefer-align-cpus-by-uncorecache` became stable in Kubernetes v1.34. A Kubelet binary running with `CompatibilityVersion=v1.30` should reject this option, but the current validation accepts it because it only checks the binary's built-in option lists.

This creates a configuration compatibility gap where a configuration accepted under version emulation would not have been accepted by an actual Kubelet of that Kubernetes release, weakening the guarantees provided by `CompatibilityVersion`.

Making policy option validation version-aware ensures that Kubelet configuration behaves consistently with the selected emulation version and preserves the expected upgrade and rollback semantics.

Title
Ensure Credential Pulled Images tests still flaking with "pulled record ... never appeared" after

Body

Hitting this on kubelet-gce-e2e-swap-ubuntu-serial - pretty sure this is the same flake as 
#136546/
#138527, just came back.

Testgrid: https://testgrid.k8s.io/[sig-redacted]#kubelet-gce-e2e-swap-ubuntu-serial

A few sub-tests under Ensure Credential Pulled Images ... [FeatureGate:KubeletEnsureSecretPulledImages] are failing, all through the same shared BeforeEach helper (tempRemoveImagePulledRecord in test/e2e_node/util_kubeletconfig.go):

util_kubeletconfig.go:133] Unexpected error: the file with the pulled record for the image ID never appeared:
<context.deadlineExceededError>: context deadline exceeded
Quick rundown of what that helper does: it polls every 1s for up to 5s waiting for kubelet to write an ImagePulledRecord at /var/lib/kubelet/image_manager/pulled/sha256-<hash>, then moves it aside so a later step can check kubelet's behavior when the record's missing. If nothing shows up in 5s, it just fails.

#138527 got closed by 
#138642, but looking at that PR, it only added debug logging to this wait loop - didn't touch the 5s timeout or actually figure out why the record's sometimes missing. So this was never really fixed, just made easier to see happening.

And that's actually how I found something new - the extra logging from 
#138642 caught this in a recent run (2026-07-25, ~12:40 UTC) that wasn't visible back when 
#138527 was filed:

util_kubeletconfig.go:116] failed to stat file ".../pulled/sha256-c0a25c4ccec43320c35febdf68a46e03b3f9323eada881535d78d91aa9962741": ... no such file or directory
util_kubeletconfig.go:128] contents of "/var/lib/kubelet/image_manager/pulled": map[
  .../pulled/sha256-fbeb66043fabeed6f125049e44aef32e0b8f9e657a240b5a2091b292bab530f2:
    {"kind":"ImagePulledRecord", ..., "lastUpdatedTime":"2026-07-25T14:26:20Z", ...}
]
So at the moment it fails, the pulled/ directory isn't actually empty - there's a record in there, just for a different image, written ~23 minutes earlier by (presumably) an earlier sub-test in the same run. The record this specific check is waiting for just never shows up in the 5s window.

That makes me think this isn't pure slowness - more likely kubelet just doesn't write a new ImagePulledRecord at all when the image's already cached from an earlier sub-test in the same run, and the poll is timing out waiting for something that was never coming. Would be good to get [sig-redacted]'s take on whether that's expected - if so, the fix is probably on the test's assumptions, not the timeout.

Checked the last 10 Testgrid columns for this job (~07-24 to 07-26) - failed 3/10 times, 6/20 over a longer window, so it's a real recurring thing, not a one-off. One specific run if useful: prow job 2080994746846679040 (2026-07-25, ~12:40-14:49 UTC), 2 sub-tests failed with this exact error.
